The ship is one slender cylinder about seven metres across, made of welded stainless-steel rings with a dull brushed finish, a smooth rounded ogive nose with no fins, two small black thruster blocks near the nose, a short row of small square windows high up, and an open rectangular crew hatch low on the hull with a narrow steel ladder running straight down to the ground. Exactly four tubular landing legs splay out from the base to wide round footpads pushed a few centimetres into the dust, a small ridge of dust shoved up on one side of each; all four touch the ground. Under the base a tight cluster of dark engine bells, cold and unlit, insides crusted with cracked grey-white residue. The hull shows its trip: heavy dark soot streaking up the lower third, straw-and-blue heat tint above the legs, shallow dents and oil-canning between the weld seams, one small scrap of crinkled silver foil lying in the dust beside a footpad. No rust, no corrugation, no conical roof; it reads as a flown spacecraft. No lettering, numbers, logos or flags anywhere. In the right middle ground, about twenty metres from the ship, two suited crew members in bulky white pressure suits with backpacks pull a small two-wheeled hand cart with thin wire wheels, loaded with three white boxes strapped down. They walk side-on to the camera, heading right, leaning into the pull, not looking at the camera. Behind the cart, two thin parallel wheel tracks run back across the grey dust to the foot of the ladder, with a scatter of ordinary-sized irregular boot prints between them; no large stamped footprint trail. The dust under the engines is scoured out radially and darker. One hard sun, low, about ten degrees above the ground, out of frame to the right. All shadows run the same way, long, sharp-edged and pure black, stretching to the left: the ship's long shadow lies across the plain far to the left, the legs, figures, cart wheels and stones each throw thin parallel shadows. The sunlit right side of the hull shows the brushed steel and soot clearly; the shadow side is very dark, lit only faintly from below by grey light thrown up from the ground. The sky is flat black with no stars, no Earth, no planet and no gradient, black all the way down to the horizon; the grey ground ends at a hard horizon line with no pale band, no glow and no haze. Camera held by a person standing about forty-five metres away, at eye height, 35mm lens, verticals level and plumb, deep focus to a sharp horizon. True colour, no added grain, no film border, no crosshair grid. No sun in frame, no lens flare or starburst, no glow in the engines, no god rays, no launch tower, gantry, pad or concrete, no second light, no gloss or stock-photo finish.
